description: Retail company with 3 sales channels (store, catalog, web). Data includes customers, items, transactions, returns, inventory, and promotions.

metrics.name: Total Revenue
metrics.definition: Sum of extended sales price across transactions
metrics.calculation: SUM(*_EXT_SALES_PRICE) from the relevant sales fact table
metrics.notes: Use SS_EXT_SALES_PRICE for store, CS_EXT_SALES_PRICE for catalog, WS_EXT_SALES_PRICE for web

metrics.name: Net Profit
metrics.definition: Revenue minus all costs (wholesale, tax, shipping, etc.)
metrics.calculation: SUM(*_NET_PROFIT) from the relevant sales fact table
metrics.notes: Can be NEGATIVE — this is expected for loss-making transactions

metrics.name: Return Rate
metrics.definition: Percentage of sold items that were returned
metrics.calculation: COUNT(returns) / COUNT(sales) for matching ticket/order numbers
metrics.notes: Must join returns back to sales on (TICKET_NUMBER + ITEM_SK) or (ORDER_NUMBER + ITEM_SK)

metrics.name: Average Transaction Value
metrics.notes: Use TICKET_NUMBER for store, ORDER_NUMBER for catalog and web

metrics.name: Customer Count
metrics.notes: CUSTOMER_SK can be NULL for anonymous/cash transactions in store sales

common_gotchas.solution: SS_CUSTOMER_SK can be NULL (anonymous transactions). Always add SS_CUSTOMER_SK IS NOT NULL when counting or joining customers.
ITEM has multiple rows per product (I_REC_START_DATE / I_REC_END_DATE). Filter I_REC_END_DATE IS NULL for current version, or join carefully on the date range.
SS_SOLD_DATE_SK is an INTEGER foreign key, not a date. Always JOIN to DATE_DIM on D_DATE_SK to get actual dates. Never do arithmetic on surrogate keys.

common_gotchas.issue: Different customer keys for billing vs shipping
common_gotchas.solution: CATALOG_SALES and WEB_SALES have both *_BILL_CUSTOMER_SK and *_SHIP_CUSTOMER_SK. They can differ (gift orders). Use BILL for revenue attribution, SHIP for logistics.

common_gotchas.issue: Fact tables can be extremely large (billions to trillions of rows)
common_gotchas.solution: ALWAYS filter by date using a CTE on DATE_DIM first (WHERE D_YEAR = ...), then join to the fact table. Never do full table scans. Always include LIMIT.
STORE_RETURNS links via SR_TICKET_NUMBER + SR_ITEM_SK. CATALOG_RETURNS via CR_ORDER_NUMBER + CR_ITEM_SK. WEB_RETURNS via WR_ORDER_NUMBER + WR_ITEM_SK.
Always use DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE_NAME for all table references to avoid ambiguity.

At petabyte scale, always pre-filter dimension tables in CTEs before joining to fact tables. Aggregate fact tables by surrogate keys first, then join to dimensions for human-readable labels. Avoid COUNT(DISTINCT) on large surrogate keys — use COUNT(*) after GROUP BY instead.

join_patterns.sales_to_date: Use CTE: WITH date_filter AS (SELECT D_DATE_SK FROM DATE_DIM WHERE D_YEAR = ...) then INNER JOIN date_filter ON <fact>.*_SOLD_DATE_SK = date_filter.D_DATE_SK
join_patterns.sales_to_item: INNER JOIN ITEM i ON <fact>.*_ITEM_SK = i.I_ITEM_SK (filter I_REC_END_DATE IS NULL for current version)
join_patterns.sales_to_customer: INNER JOIN CUSTOMER c ON <fact>.*_CUSTOMER_SK = c.C_CUSTOMER_SK (ensure *_CUSTOMER_SK IS NOT NULL)
join_patterns.sales_to_store: INNER JOIN STORE s ON ss.SS_STORE_SK = s.S_STORE_SK
join_patterns.customer_to_address: INNER JOIN CUSTOMER_ADDRESS ca ON c.C_CURRENT_ADDR_SK = ca.CA_ADDRESS_SK
join_patterns.customer_to_demographics: INNER JOIN CUSTOMER_DEMOGRAPHICS cd ON c.C_CURRENT_CDEMO_SK = cd.CD_DEMO_SK
join_patterns.returns_to_sales_store: INNER JOIN STORE_SALES ss ON sr.SR_TICKET_NUMBER = ss.SS_TICKET_NUMBER AND sr.SR_ITEM_SK = ss.SS_ITEM_SK
join_patterns.returns_to_sales_catalog: INNER JOIN CATALOG_SALES cs ON cr.CR_ORDER_NUMBER = cs.CS_ORDER_NUMBER AND cr.CR_ITEM_SK = cs.CS_ITEM_SK
join_patterns.returns_to_sales_web: INNER JOIN WEB_SALES ws ON wr.WR_ORDER_NUMBER = ws.WS_ORDER_NUMBER AND wr.WR_ITEM_SK = ws.WS_ITEM_SK
